comment: D65/D69: the pinned C toolchain native build scripts run with (clang, libclang, llvm-ar), the LLVM project's own release of the LLVM version llvm.json pins (23.1.4) until our fork's archive carries a clang (.github/scripts/llvm.py). Read by blaze_build_script::native::pin. `sysroots`: the C library headers per target; macOS takes the machine's SDK by version and the headers read (D69), Linux a pinned glibc sysroot: none pinned yet (null).
version_text_comment: Brief P: what the pinned clang prints as its first `--version` line is `clang version <version> (<repository> <revision>)`; both read from the macOS archive's bin/clang-23 (its baked VCS repository and revision). Read by blaze_build_script::fact_pins.
shelf_programs_comment: shelf-pins: each program placed on a host's shelf, pinned one by one beside the archive's digest: per program row, `member` is its path in the archive and `sha256` the member's own SHA-256; its place on the shelf is the member without the archive's top folder (one of blaze_build_script::toolchain::SHELF_MEMBERS). The step that places a program checks the extracted member against its row and refuses it by name when no row pins it or the digest differs (blaze_build_script::shelf_pins::place_member). A host tool's `shelf` names one of these rows. `names` is sorted and each row's last field.
host_tools_comment: D71: the only programs other than the C toolchain a native build script may start, per host target. `names`: the tools, space-separated, sorted. Per tool: `path`, the resolved real path (no link), granted read and execute; `reads`, space-separated folders its runtime needs, granted read-only (perl: libperl.dylib, privlib and archlib are /System/Library/Perl/<v>, vendorlib /System/Library/Perl/Extras/<v>, from libperl's own Config.pm; the site folder /Library/Perl is NOT granted: user-installed modules are not keyed); `runs`, space-separated real paths of the programs the tool itself starts, granted execute and each keyed by its digest (perl's piped `open` of a command with a quote in it, as cryptogams' keccak1600-armv8.pl opens arm-xlate.pl, starts /bin/sh, which reads the link /private/var/select/sh and starts /bin/bash on this host); `needed_by`, the scripts' packages known to start it, space-separated, sorted; `runs_out_dir`, yes or no: whether the tool starts programs the script wrote under its OUT_DIR, so the script's sandbox may start anything there and the pinned linker (D112: sh runs tikv-jemalloc-sys's configure, which compiles, links and runs its test programs). nm-row: a row gives its program either as `path` (on the machine) or as `shelf` (the name of its program's row in `shelf_programs`, which pins the archive member by digest and gives its place on the shelf; a tool with no row cannot be granted, shelf-pins: nm is the row llvm-nm, the shelf's bin/llvm-nm, from the same LLVM as its clang and lld, never the machine's /usr/bin/nm xcrun shim); `env`, where given, is the variable the script is told the program's real path in (NM), and that row's folder is not on PATH; a shelf row must give one. make is the real binary xcrun resolves /usr/bin/make to (the shim and xcrun are not granted); make's runs are what jemalloc's Makefile.in recipes start with no shell (GNU make execs a recipe line holding no shell syntax directly: `@mkdir -p`, `rm -f`, `ln -sf`, `echo`, `@touch`, `@true`, `$(INSTALL)`); sh's runs are what jemalloc's configure, config.sub, Makefile recipes and include scripts start, read from their text. The tool's binary digest and its row's `runs_out_dir` are in the run key and the record is marked `host-tool`: it never enters the shared cache. `interim`: a row whose grant widens the sandbox (runs_out_dir yes) says it holds only for D112's interim, records local (checked by host_tools' tests). Read by blaze_build_script::host_tools.

sh.interim: D112 interim: this row's grant (sh may start what the script wrote under OUT_DIR and the script's links use the shelf's bin/ld64.lld and bin/lld) holds only until the deterministic sandbox runs build scripts; its records stay local (marked host-tool) and are never offered to a shared cache

aarch64-apple-darwin.names: hostname make nm perl sh uname
